security.rationale: Scheme-relative URL would navigate to another origin; must be rejected.
Embedded scheme separator; must be rejected.
Absolute URL to another origin; must be rejected.
Script URL; must be rejected (does not start with "/").
Dot segments can leave the product path once a host joins the route to a base URL; the protocol accepts it, hosts must not resolve it outside the product origin/path.
Whitespace in a route; accepted by the protocol, refused by Compute. Hosts building URLs must encode, not concatenate.
Backslash is treated as a path separator by WHATWG URL parsing in browsers; accepted by the protocol.
A query in a route lets a product steer parameters of the host-built link; accepted by the protocol.
A fragment in a route; accepted by the protocol.
A control character in a route; accepted by the protocol.
